summary: The study investigates the resistive switching behavior of NiO thin films prepared through atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films were deposited using Ni(dmamb)2 as a nickel precursor and water as an oxygen source at 140 °C. Impedance spectroscopy was used to analyze the electrical and dielectric properties, revealing that the resistive switching originates from bulk-related responses rather than interfacial effects. The low dielectric constant and bias-independent capacitance support the bulk-based switching mechanism.
evidence: NiO thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) which used Ni(dmamb)2 as a Ni precursor, where dmamb is described as 1-dimethylamino-2-methyl-2-butanolate and water as an oxygen source.15 Two amorphous NiO thin films, 40 and 190 nm, were deposited onto commercial Pt-coated wafers at 140 °C.
